medtop:20000711.definition: The scientific manipulation of living organisms and biological processes for scientific, medical or agricultural purposes

medtop:20000712.name: dentistry
medtop:20000712.definition: The medical profession and field of study devoted to diagnosing, preventing and treating oral conditions

medtop:20000714.name: veterinary medicine
medtop:20000714.definition: The medical profession and field of study devoted to diagnosis, prevention and treatment of medical conditions in animals

medtop:20000715.name: mathematics
medtop:20000715.definition: The study of structure, space, change and number in abstract, often using symbolic logic and language, and including subjects such as geometry, algebra or trigonometry

medtop:20000716.name: mechanical engineering
medtop:20000716.definition: The study and application of the design, construction and operation of mechanical systems

medtop:20000717.name: natural science
medtop:20000717.definition: The sciences that deal with matter, energy and the physical world, including physics, biology, chemistry and astronomy

medtop:20000718.name: astronomy
medtop:20000718.definition: The study of celestial objects through direct observation and theoretical models

medtop:20000719.name: biology
medtop:20000719.definition: The study of the anatomy, behaviour, origin, physiology and other aspects of living organisms

medtop:20000720.name: botany
medtop:20000720.definition: The study of the physical and physiological structure, genetics, ecology and other aspects of plants

medtop:20000721.name: genetics
medtop:20000721.definition: The study of genes in living organisms, and of their role in heredity, development or genetic adaptation

medtop:20000722.name: palaeontology
medtop:20000722.definition: The study of prehistoric life forms, geological periods and fossils

medtop:20000723.name: physiology
medtop:20000723.definition: The study of the vital processes, internal organs or functional mechanisms of living organisms

medtop:20000724.name: zoology
medtop:20000724.definition: The study of the biology, physiology, development, behaviour or other aspects of animals

medtop:20000725.name: chemistry
medtop:20000725.definition: The study of the composition and properties of matter on the scale of atoms and molecules, and of the reactions between compounds

medtop:20000726.name: cosmology
medtop:20000726.definition: The study of the origin, evolution, organisation and structure of the universe

medtop:20000727.name: geology
medtop:20000727.definition: The study of Earth's physical processes, material structures and its properties

medtop:20000728.name: horticulture
medtop:20000728.definition: The study and art of plant cultivation, including landscape and garden design and plant conservation

medtop:20000729.name: marine science
medtop:20000729.definition: The study of living organisms and environments in saltwater ecosystems

medtop:20000730.name: meteorology
medtop:20000730.definition: The study of atmospheric chemistry and physics, with a focus on weather forecasting

medtop:20000731.name: physics
medtop:20000731.definition: The study of the movement and structure of matter, and how it relates to energy

medtop:20000732.name: electromagnetism
medtop:20000732.definition: The study of the physical interactions between electrically charged particles and magnetic fields

medtop:20000733.name: nuclear physics
medtop:20000733.definition: The study of the structure and behaviour of atomic nuclei

medtop:20000734.name: particle physics
medtop:20000734.definition: The study of the nature, properties and interactions of the elementary particles that constitute matter

medtop:20000735.name: scientific research
medtop:20000735.definition: The scientific and methodical investigation of events, procedures and interactions to explain why they occur, or to find solutions for problems

medtop:20000736.name: scientific innovation
medtop:20000736.definition: The development or creation of new scientific or technological products or processes, such as biotech or artificial intelligence applications, robotic limbs or nanoscale cameras

medtop:20000737.name: medical research
medtop:20000737.definition: Investigation conducted in the fields of health and medicine, such as genetic studies, disease research or pharmaceutical drug trials

medtop:20000738.name: scientific exploration
medtop:20000738.definition: Land, sea or space journeys undertaken to discover new information

medtop:20000739.name: space exploration
medtop:20000739.definition: The scientific exploration of outer space through manned and unmanned missions

medtop:20000740.name: scientific publication
medtop:20000740.definition: Academic research findings published in a journal, book or thesis

medtop:20000741.name: scientific institution
medtop:20000741.definition: Institution that carries out or governs scientific work, such as the National Academy of Arts and Sciences

medtop:20000742.name: social sciences
medtop:20000742.definition: The study of human society in such aspects as linguistics, anthropology, economics or sociology

medtop:20000743.name: anthropology
medtop:20000743.definition: The study of human behaviour and social interactions across time

medtop:20000744.name: archaeology
medtop:20000744.definition: The study of human activity throughout time and cultural history, using artefacts left behind by ancient peoples

medtop:20000745.name: economics
medtop:20000745.definition: The study of the laws and principles of economies, such as the production and distribution of goods and services

medtop:20000746.name: geography
medtop:20000746.definition: The study of the physical features of the surface of Earth and its political divisions

medtop:20000747.name: history
medtop:20000747.definition: The study of human events of the past

medtop:20000748.name: information science
medtop:20000748.definition: The study and practice of collecting, classifying, storing, retrieving and disseminating information

medtop:20000749.name: study of law
medtop:20000749.definition: The study of legal systems and the philosophy of law

medtop:20000750.name: linguistics
medtop:20000750.definition: The study of all aspects of human language such as syntax, phonetics, written and spoken forms and variations over time

medtop:20000751.name: philosophy
medtop:20000751.definition: The study of the principles and fundamental questions about matters such as the mind, reason, morality or values

medtop:20000752.name: political science
medtop:20000752.definition: The study of the principles of political and governmental systems, political thought and practices

medtop:20000753.name: psychology
medtop:20000753.definition: The study of the human mind, mental characteristics and emotional processes

medtop:20000754.name: sociology
medtop:20000754.definition: The study of human social organisation, social relationships and societal changes

medtop:20000755.name: scientific standards
medtop:20000755.definition: Nationally or internationally established rules governing scientific and technological study and development, such as calibration standards for scientific tools or equipment

medtop:20000756.name: technology and engineering
medtop:20000756.definition: The study and practice of industrial or applied sciences such as physics, hydrodynamics or thermodynamics

medtop:20000757.name: aerospace engineering
medtop:20000757.definition: The study, design, development and construction of aircraft, spacecraft and missile systems

medtop:20000758.name: rocketry
medtop:20000758.definition: The study, design, development and construction of rockets

medtop:20000759.name: agricultural technology
medtop:20000759.definition: The study and development of techniques and machinery to improve agricultural management and productivity

medtop:20000760.name: civil engineering
medtop:20000760.definition: The study, design, development and construction of structures such as buildings, bridges, tunnels, irrigation and sewage systems, streets or railroads

medtop:20000761.name: electronic engineering
medtop:20000761.definition: The study, design, development and application of systems built on the exchange of electrical charges, such as consumer devices, communications systems or industrial computers

medtop:20000762.name: identification technology
medtop:20000762.definition: The study, development, application and ethical considerations of technological methods for identifying products, animals or people; including radio frequency, biometrics or face recognition

medtop:20000763.name: information technology and computer science
medtop:20000763.definition: The study and design of computer systems, software and networks

medtop:20000764.name: materials science
medtop:20000764.definition: The study of the composition, structure and properties of materials for their use in industry and manufacturing

medtop:20000765.name: micro science
medtop:20000765.definition: The study of and technologies built at a microscopic scale, such as microbiology or microcomputing

medtop:20000766.name: nanotechnology
medtop:20000766.definition: Manipulating objects at the molecular scale

medtop:20000768.name: communities
medtop:20000768.definition: A group of individuals actively sharing a common value or interest

medtop:20000769.name: social networking
medtop:20000769.definition: Social interactions, either in person or online, intended to share information and build relationships around common interests

medtop:20000770.name: demographics
medtop:20000770.definition: The study of human populations and their characteristics, for example statistics or trends around aging populations in a particular geographic region

medtop:20000771.name: immigration
medtop:20000771.definition: The movement of individuals or groups of people from one country to another

medtop:20000772.name: emigration
medtop:20000772.definition: Leaving one's country of residence to settle permanently elsewhere

medtop:20000773.name: illegal immigration
medtop:20000773.definition: The movement of individuals or groups of people from one country to another without legal authorisation from the destination country

medtop:20000774.name: population and census
medtop:20000774.definition: The official count of people living in a given geopolitical area, usually carried out by a governmental body

medtop:20000775.name: discrimination
medtop:20000775.definition: Unfair treatment of, or policies or practices against, individuals or groups of people on the basis of real or perceived membership in a group, such as race, sexual orientation, political or religious beliefs, age or height

medtop:20000776.name: ageism
medtop:20000776.definition: Discrimination against individuals or groups of people on the basis of age

medtop:20000777.name: racism
medtop:20000777.definition: Discrimination against individuals or groups of people on the basis of race

medtop:20000778.name: religious discrimination
medtop:20000778.definition: Unfair treatment of individuals or groups of people on the basis of their religious belief

medtop:20000779.name: sexism
medtop:20000779.definition: Discrimination against individuals or groups of people, usually women, on the basis of gender

medtop:20000780.name: family
medtop:20000780.definition: A group of people related genetically or by a legal bond, or who consider themselves part of a familial unit regardless of genetic or legal status

medtop:20000781.name: adoption
medtop:20000781.definition: The legal process of transferring parental rights to someone other than a person's birth parents, that person usually being a child

medtop:20000782.name: Dating and Relationships
medtop:20000782.definition: The development of an intimate connection between individuals, through various forms of activities enjoyed together, often leading to a legal or permanent union such as marriage

medtop:20000783.name: divorce
medtop:20000783.definition: The process by which a marriage is legally dissolved

medtop:20000784.name: family planning
medtop:20000784.definition: Services and education aimed at informing individual decisions about reproduction, such as fertility, in vitro fertilisation, contraception or abortion

medtop:20000785.name: abortion
medtop:20000785.definition: The intentional termination of a pregnancy for elective or medical reasons

medtop:20000786.name: marriage
medtop:20000786.definition: The legal or socially recognised union of individuals, which establishes rights and obligations between them

medtop:20000787.name: parenting
medtop:20000787.definition: The caring for and support of a child's physical, emotional, developmental and social needs from birth to adulthood

medtop:20000788.name: demographic group
medtop:20000788.definition: A subset of society with shared traits

medtop:20000789.name: adults
medtop:20000789.definition: People above an age set by law that entitles them to full liability and certain privileges such as the legal right to drink alcoholic beverages and to vote

medtop:20000790.name: children
medtop:20000790.definition: Young people, usually pre-pubescent, who are legally considered minors and are in a guardianship relationship with adults

medtop:20000791.name: disabilities
medtop:20000791.definition: Physical or mental conditions that limit a person's movements, senses, or activities

medtop:20000792.name: LGBTQ
medtop:20000792.definition: People who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer

medtop:20000793.name: gender
medtop:20000793.definition: The classification of individuals as male, female, or a non-binary designation

medtop:20000794.name: infants
medtop:20000794.definition: Very young people, usually defined as being just born up to the age of two

medtop:20000795.name: national or ethnic minority
medtop:20000795.definition: Groups of people that form a minority on an ethnic or national basis, and their status or issues relating to the majority

medtop:20000797.name: senior citizens
medtop:20000797.definition: People having passed the age of retirement

medtop:20000798.name: teenagers
medtop:20000798.definition: Young people between the ages that describe childhood and adulthood

medtop:20000799.name: social condition
medtop:20000799.definition: The circumstances or state of affairs affecting a person's life, welfare and relations with others in a society

medtop:20000800.name: homelessness
medtop:20000800.definition: The social condition defined by lack of permanent residence, living in shelters or on streets, and the issues and problems associated with it

medtop:20000801.name: poverty
medtop:20000801.definition: The lack of sufficient resources and means to provide basic needs such as food, clothing or shelter for oneself and one's family

medtop:20000802.name: social problem
medtop:20000802.definition: Issues related to human rights, human welfare and other areas of societal concern

medtop:20000803.name: abusive behaviour
medtop:20000803.definition: Actions that intentionally harm another person or people, often on an ongoing basis, such as psychological or mental abuse, negligence, physical or sexual abuse and torture

medtop:20000804.name: addiction
medtop:20000804.definition: The habitual and compulsive use of substances such as alcohol or drugs, or behaviour such as gambling, gaming or sex, often causing detrimental effects on the body, brain, and relationships with others

medtop:20000805.name: juvenile delinquency
medtop:20000805.definition: Unlawful conduct perpetrated by minors, often on a repeated basis

medtop:20000806.name: prostitution
medtop:20000806.definition: The business of engaging in sexual activity in exchange for payment

medtop:20000807.name: slavery
medtop:20000807.definition: The ownership of people as property, and the involuntary servitude of those people to their owners, which includes unpaid labour and coerced actions

medtop:20000808.name: values
medtop:20000808.definition: A person's or group's principles or standards of behaviour, which guide their way of living and choices made

medtop:20000810.name: death and dying
medtop:20000810.definition: Social, medical and mental health issues relating to people at the end of their lives

medtop:20000811.name: euthanasia
medtop:20000811.definition: The practice of humanely ending the life of a person suffering from a terminal illness

medtop:20000812.name: assisted suicide
medtop:20000812.definition: The practice of assisting a person suffering from a terminal illness in the process of suicide, often with a physician's oversight

medtop:20000813.name: suicide
medtop:20000813.definition: The intentional taking of one's own life

medtop:20000814.name: ethics
medtop:20000814.definition: The moral values and standards that define right and wrong actions or decisions

medtop:20000815.name: pornography
medtop:20000815.definition: The depiction of sexually explicit acts in various media renditions, such as video or photos, often considered obscene or immoral

medtop:20000816.name: sexual behaviour
medtop:20000816.definition: The manner in which people express their sexuality in physical acts

medtop:20000817.name: welfare
medtop:20000817.definition: Help for those in need of food, housing, health and other services

medtop:20000818.name: charity
medtop:20000818.definition: The voluntary giving of money, food or other necessities to those in need

medtop:20000819.name: long-term care
medtop:20000819.definition: Services provided on an extended and ongoing basis to patients suffering from chronic illness or disability

medtop:20000820.name: social services
medtop:20000820.definition: Social programmes, usually publicly sponsored, aimed at promoting people's welfare, such as housing, health care or education services

medtop:20000822.name: competitive sport
medtop:20000822.definition: Sports and their disciplines executed in competitions

medtop:20000823.name: American football
medtop:20000823.definition: Team ball game that opposes two teams of 11 that have offensive and defensive players. Each offence attempts to move an oval ball down the 120-yard-long field. Points are scored by advancing the ball into the opposing team's end zone.

medtop:20000824.name: archery
medtop:20000824.definition: Archers use bows and arrows to aim at targets, includes longbow and crossbow

medtop:20000827.name: athletics
medtop:20000827.definition: Competitions involving foot races, jumping, and throwing which can be on a track inside a stadium or on outside roads

medtop:20000828.name: cross-country running
medtop:20000828.definition: Competitors run over rough ground and not on a track

medtop:20000829.name: decathlon
medtop:20000829.definition: Individual men's competition which involves accumulating points in ten different disciplines over two days

medtop:20000830.name: discus throw
medtop:20000830.definition: Competitors stand in a netted circle and attempt to throw a discus as far as possible

medtop:20000831.name: hammer throw
medtop:20000831.definition: Competitors throw a hammer consisting of a metal ball, chain and handle as far as they can from a netted circle

medtop:20000832.name: heptathlon
medtop:20000832.definition: Individual women's competition which involves accumulating points in seven separate disciplines over two days

medtop:20000833.name: high jump
medtop:20000833.definition: Competitors build up speed over a short sprint and then jump as high as possible over a horizontal bar

medtop:20000834.name: hurdles
medtop:20000834.definition: A sprint running race where athletes jump over a series of upright frames

medtop:20000835.name: javelin throw
medtop:20000835.definition: Competitors in a specially-designated throwing area attempt to throw a javelin as far as possible

medtop:20000836.name: long distance running
medtop:20000836.definition: A running race at distances of more than 1500 metres

medtop:20000837.name: long jump
medtop:20000837.definition: Competitors build up speed over a short sprint and then jump in one leap as far as possible

medtop:20000838.name: middle distance running
medtop:20000838.definition: A running race at distances of more than 400 metres and up to and including 1500 metres

medtop:20000840.name: pole vault
medtop:20000840.definition: Competitors use a flexible pole to propel themselves into the air and clear a bar which is raised higher at each round of jumps

medtop:20000841.name: race walking
medtop:20000841.definition: A race requiring the competitor to have always one foot on the ground

medtop:20000842.name: relay running
medtop:20000842.definition: A team of athletes run a relay over identical distances

medtop:20000843.name: shot put
medtop:20000843.definition: Competitors stand in a circle and attempt to throw a metal ball as far as possible

medtop:20000844.name: sprinting
medtop:20000844.definition: A running race at distances of up to and including 400 metres

medtop:20000845.name: triple jump
medtop:20000845.definition: Competitors build up speed over a short sprint and then attempt to jump as far forward as they can using a hop, skip and jump technique

medtop:20000846.name: Australian rules football
medtop:20000846.definition: A form of football played by two teams of 18 competing on a pitch by running with, kicking and passing an oval ball. Points are scored by moving the ball between goal posts.

medtop:20000847.name: badminton
medtop:20000847.definition: Two players or two teams of two compete by hitting a shuttlecock over a high net

medtop:20000848.name: bandy
medtop:20000848.definition: Ice sport, similar to ice hockey, using a hard ball instead of a puck

medtop:20000849.name: baseball
medtop:20000849.definition: A bat and ball game between two teams of nine played on a field with a diamond shaped circuit of four bases

medtop:20000851.name: basketball
medtop:20000851.definition: Two teams of five players score points by shooting a ball through the opponent's hoop

medtop:20000852.name: biathlon
medtop:20000852.definition: A combination of cross-country skiing and target shooting in a pursuit format

medtop:20000853.name: billiards
medtop:20000853.definition: A cue sport with balls on a table without a specific order to play them

medtop:20000854.name: bobsleigh
medtop:20000854.definition: One, two or four people seated in a gravity-powered sled racing down a narrow winding course

medtop:20000855.name: boules
medtop:20000855.definition: Collective name of a number of games where the common goal is to move the competitor's balls as close to a small target ball as possible, played on a grass or sand surface. Balls are thrown (as in petanque and boules) or rolled (as in lawn bowls or bocce).

medtop:20000856.name: boxing
medtop:20000856.definition: Combat sport in which two competitors fight using only their fists covered by padded gloves in a square ring

medtop:20000875.name: bullfighting
medtop:20000875.definition: A physical contest that involves a bullfighter attempting to subdue, immobilise, or kill a bull

medtop:20000876.name: Canadian football
medtop:20000876.definition: Team ball game that opposes two teams of 12 that have offensive and defensive players. Each offence attempts to move an oval ball down the 150 yards long field. Points are scored by advancing the ball into the opposing team's end zone.

medtop:20000877.name: canoeing
medtop:20000877.definition: Competition involving canoes which are generally kneeled and paddled with a single-bladed paddle

medtop:20000883.name: casting (fishing)
medtop:20000883.definition: Using fishing equipment to hit a target and score points

medtop:20000887.name: sport climbing
medtop:20000887.definition: Rock climbing that uses pre-drilled, permanent metal bolts fixed into rock or a wall

medtop:20000888.name: cricket
medtop:20000888.definition: Ball sport involving two teams of 11 players, balls, bats, and wickets. The aim is to score as many runs as possible, and to get the opposing team 'out.'

medtop:20000889.name: croquet
medtop:20000889.definition: A sport using mallets to hit a ball through wickets

medtop:20000890.name: curling
medtop:20000890.definition: A game played on ice with large flat round stones. A player throws the stone, aiming at a target. Teammates of the player who has thrown the stone can sweep the ice in front of the stone to help smooth its path towards the target.

medtop:20000891.name: icestock sport
medtop:20000891.definition: A game where competitors slide ice stocks over an ice surface, aiming for a target, or to cover the longest distance

medtop:20000892.name: cycling
medtop:20000892.definition: Sports involving bicycles, including races, tricks, and team competitions

medtop:20000893.name: artistic cycling
medtop:20000893.definition: A form of competitive cycling in which athletes perform tricks for points on specialised, fixed gear bikes in an arena

medtop:20000895.name: bmx racing
medtop:20000895.definition: Bicycle racing with an inline start and various obstacles over off-road circuits

medtop:20000896.name: cycle ball
medtop:20000896.definition: Competitive team sport using bicycles where competitors aim to move the ball using the front and rear wheels without letting their feet touch the ground

medtop:20000903.name: mountain biking
medtop:20000903.definition: All-terrain, off-road bicycle riding requiring endurance and specially adapted mountain bikes

medtop:20000911.name: competitive dancing
medtop:20000911.definition: Dancing competition where competitors are judged on technique and interpretation

medtop:20000912.name: darts
medtop:20000912.definition: Competitors throw darts at a dartboard, a circular target divided into numbered sections

medtop:20000913.name: diving
medtop:20000913.definition: Competitors dive off a fixed or spring board and are assessed by judges on their execution

medtop:20000914.name: platform diving
medtop:20000914.definition: Competitors dive from a high platform

medtop:20000915.name: springboard diving
medtop:20000915.definition: Competitors dive from a high springboard

medtop:20000916.name: synchronised diving
medtop:20000916.definition: Two competitors from the same team dive off at the same time from separate platforms or springboards. As well as being judged on the standard criteria they are also awarded marks for synchronisation.

medtop:20000917.name: scuba diving
medtop:20000917.definition: Underwater diving with the use of a self-contained underwater breathing apparatus

medtop:20000922.name: duathlon
medtop:20000922.definition: An athletic event involving running and cycling

medtop:20000923.name: equestrian
medtop:20000923.definition: Horse-based sport disciplines governed by the International Federation for Equestrian Sports, such as dressage, eventing, show jumping and vaulting

medtop:20000929.name: fencing
medtop:20000929.definition: Combat sport using a sword or foil

medtop:20000933.name: hockey
medtop:20000933.definition: A ball sport involving two teams of 11 players using curved sticks

medtop:20000934.name: figure skating
medtop:20000934.definition: Competitors skate to music and are judged on artistic flair and technical precision

medtop:20000936.name: fistball
medtop:20000936.definition: Men's team sport similar to volleyball primarily played in Austria, Germany, Switzerland, and Brazil

medtop:20000937.name: floorball
medtop:20000937.definition: Teams of 6 players use plastic clubs and a light plastic ball to score goals

medtop:20000938.name: flying disc sport
medtop:20000938.definition: A group of events all played with a flying plastic disc, such as disc golf and ultimate frisbee

medtop:20000939.name: Gaelic football
medtop:20000939.definition: A form of football played by two teams of 15 competing on a pitch by running with, kicking and passing a spherical ball. Points are scored by moving the ball between goal posts.

medtop:20000940.name: golf
medtop:20000940.definition: A game in which players hit a small, hard ball into a series of holes in as few strokes as possible on a large outdoor course

medtop:20000941.name: mini golf
medtop:20000941.definition: A game in which players hit a small, hard ball into a series of holes in as few strokes as possible on an small articfical course often containing hazards

medtop:20000942.name: gymnastics
medtop:20000942.definition: A sport consisting of a variety of disciplines in which gymnasts perform artistic and acrobatic moves using different apparatus

medtop:20000951.name: rhythmic gymnastics
medtop:20000951.definition: Competitors perform a mixture of dance and gymnastic moves and are judged on technical ability and artistic expression

medtop:20000955.name: trampoline
medtop:20000955.definition: Competitors perform gymnastic moves whilst bouncing on a trampoline

medtop:20000958.name: handball
medtop:20000958.definition: A ball game in which two teams of seven try to throw a ball into an opponent's goal

medtop:20000960.name: horse racing
medtop:20000960.definition: An equestrian race involving two or more horses ridden by jockeys or driven by drivers over a set distance

medtop:20000965.name: ice hockey
medtop:20000965.definition: Two teams of six heavily padded skaters try and outscore each other by hitting a puck into the opponent's goal

medtop:20000968.name: Jai Alai (Pelota)
medtop:20000968.definition: A fast-paced ball sport played using either the bare hand or a wicker scoop in a walled arena

medtop:20000969.name: judo
medtop:20000969.definition: A defensive martial art of Japanese origin characterised by throwing, pinning, and submitting opponents using principles of balance, leverage, and action-reaction

medtop:20000977.name: jukendo
medtop:20000977.definition: Japanese traditional martial art using a model rifle made of wood

medtop:20000978.name: kabaddi
medtop:20000978.definition: Team based contact sport popular in South Asia

medtop:20000979.name: kayaking
medtop:20000979.definition: Watersport in which paddlers in kayaks race against the clock

medtop:20000983.name: karate
medtop:20000983.definition: A Japanese martial art where chops, punches, kicks and throws are used to defeat an opponent

medtop:20000984.name: kendo
medtop:20000984.definition: Japanese traditional martial art using a bamboo sword, sometimes called Japanese fencing

medtop:20000985.name: kyudo
medtop:20000985.definition: Japanese traditional martial art using a bamboo bow and arrows, sometimes called Japanese archery

medtop:20000986.name: lacrosse
medtop:20000986.definition: Two teams of players use netted sticks to try to launch a hard ball into a goal

medtop:20000987.name: luge
medtop:20000987.definition: Competitors lay on their back feet first on an open sled and race down a course

medtop:20000989.name: modern pentathlon
medtop:20000989.definition: Five events run over a single day in the following order: shooting, fencing, swimming, horse riding and running

medtop:20000990.name: motorboat racing
medtop:20000990.definition: Racing boats with engines on lakes, rivers or the ocean

medtop:20000991.name: motor racing
medtop:20000991.definition: Car racing governed by a set of rules and regulations, for example Formula 1 and NASCAR

medtop:20000998.name: motorcycle racing
medtop:20000998.definition: motorcycle racing governed by a set of rules and regulations, for example Grand Prix and MotoGP

medtop:20001009.name: naginata
medtop:20001009.definition: Japanese traditional martial art using a pole sword made of wood

medtop:20001010.name: netball
medtop:20001010.definition: Sport primarily played by women that is similar to basketball, but has no contact and no board behind the hoop

medtop:20001011.name: orienteering
medtop:20001011.definition: An individual time-trial over a route marked out by beacons that the competitor has to search out and find in a specific order with the help of a compass and map

medtop:20001012.name: ski orienteering
medtop:20001012.definition: An individual ski time-trial over a route marked out by beacons that the competitor has to search out and find in a specific order with the help of a compass and map

medtop:20001013.name: parachuting and skydiving
medtop:20001013.definition: Jumping from an aeroplane using a parachute. Participants are evaluated on factors such as, formation, style, speed and accuracy.

medtop:20001014.name: polo
medtop:20001014.definition: With the aid of a mallet, two teams of four players on horseback try and knock a bamboo ball into the opponent's goal over a pitch

medtop:20001015.name: pool
medtop:20001015.definition: A cue sport on a table with pockets, played with different numbers of balls

medtop:20001017.name: rodeo
medtop:20001017.definition: A discipline where wild horses or bulls must be mounted and mastered

medtop:20001025.name: roller hockey
medtop:20001025.definition: Team sport similar to ice hockey, executed on wheeled skates with sticks and a ball

medtop:20001026.name: rowing
medtop:20001026.definition: Boat racing usually on flat, calm waters with boats for 1, 2, 4 or 8 rowers

medtop:20001035.name: rugby league
medtop:20001035.definition: A type of rugby where two teams of 13 compete on a pitch by running with and passing an oval ball. Points are scored by touching down the ball behind the goal line or kicking it between goal posts.

medtop:20001036.name: rugby union
medtop:20001036.definition: A type of rugby where two teams of 15 compete on a pitch by running with and passing an oval ball. Points are scored by touching down the ball behind the goal line or kicking it between goal posts.

medtop:20001037.name: rugby sevens
medtop:20001037.definition: A type of rugby union where two teams of 7 compete on a pitch by running with and passing an oval ball. Points are scored by touching down the ball behind the goal line or kicking it between goal posts.

medtop:20001038.name: sailing
medtop:20001038.definition: Sail boat racing over a closed course or going from point to point

medtop:20001047.name: sepak takraw
medtop:20001047.definition: A volleyball-like game where players must not use their hands

medtop:20001048.name: shinty
medtop:20001048.definition: A ball game involving 2 teams with curved sticks called camans

medtop:20001049.name: sport shooting
medtop:20001049.definition: Using firearms to hit stationary or moving targets

medtop:20001055.name: skeleton
medtop:20001055.definition: Competitors lie on their stomachs on a sled while racing down a frozen track

medtop:20001056.name: skiing
medtop:20001056.definition: A winter sport involving gliding on skis on flat or downhill snow covered surfaces

medtop:20001057.name: alpine skiing
medtop:20001057.definition: Racing downhill on snow-covered slopes using skis with fixed-heel bindings

medtop:20001058.name: freestyle skiing
medtop:20001058.definition: Skiing competitions which incorporate acrobatic moves and jumps. Events include aerials, halfpipe, slopestyle, ski cross, moguls and big air.

medtop:20001061.name: ski jumping
medtop:20001061.definition: Competitors descend a snow covered elevated ramp on skis and try to fly off it as far as possible, receiving marks for distance, style of flight and landing

medtop:20001063.name: snooker
medtop:20001063.definition: A cue sport with balls on a table to be potted in a specific order

medtop:20001064.name: snowboarding
medtop:20001064.definition: Descending a snow-covered surface using a single board

medtop:20001065.name: football
medtop:20001065.definition: Also known as soccer. Played by two teams competing on a pitch by kicking a spherical ball. Points are scored by kicking or heading the ball into a goal. Governed by the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA).

medtop:20001066.name: softball
medtop:20001066.definition: Similar to baseball but with a larger and softer ball, a thinner bat, shorter gaps between bases and less innings

medtop:20001067.name: speed skating
medtop:20001067.definition: Timed races with two or more skaters at a time competing on an oval ice track

medtop:20001068.name: squash and racquetball
medtop:20001068.definition: A racquet sport played by singles or doubles teams in a walled court with a small rubber ball

medtop:20001069.name: sumo wrestling
medtop:20001069.definition: A combat sport where two contestants try to throw or slap a competitor out of a marked area

medtop:20001070.name: surfing
medtop:20001070.definition: Water sport where participants catch and ride waves on a surfboard

medtop:20001071.name: swimming
medtop:20001071.definition: A water sport where participants race using a specific stroke style

medtop:20001077.name: marathon swimming
medtop:20001077.definition: Water sport where competitors race a minimum distance of 10 kilometers in natural bodies of water

medtop:20001083.name: table tennis
medtop:20001083.definition: A racquet sport where two or four players (in doubles) compete at a table divided by a net

medtop:20001084.name: Taekwon-Do
medtop:20001084.definition: A martial art of Korean origin characterised by fast, high, spinning kicks

medtop:20001085.name: tennis
medtop:20001085.definition: A sport where two players, or four in doubles, use a racquet to hit a ball over a net into the opponent's side of the court with the aim of putting it out of reach within the regulation lines

medtop:20001086.name: tenpin bowling
medtop:20001086.definition: A game in which a player scores points by trying to knock down ten pins using a weighted ball

medtop:20001087.name: triathlon
medtop:20001087.definition: An endurance multi-sport where competitors first swim, then cycle and then run a road race. Distances vary according to the competition.

medtop:20001089.name: volleyball
medtop:20001089.definition: Two teams of six hit a ball over a net into the opponent's half of the court keeping the ball in the air at all times

medtop:20001090.name: beach volleyball
medtop:20001090.definition: Two teams of two players compete on a sand court

medtop:20001091.name: water polo
medtop:20001091.definition: Water sport played in a pool between two teams of 7, who must stay afloat and use only one hand to pass the ball or swim with it before throwing it into the opponent's net

medtop:20001092.name: water skiing
medtop:20001092.definition: Participants are pulled by a power boat along the water's surface while balancing on skis

medtop:20001093.name: weightlifting and powerlifting

medtop:20001097.name: windsurfing

medtop:20001103.name: disciplinary action in sport

medtop:20001104.name: drug use in sport

medtop:20001108.name: sport event

medtop:20001125.name: sport organisation

medtop:20001126.name: sport venue

medtop:20001128.name: weather forecast

medtop:20001129.name: weather phenomena
medtop:20001129.definition: Short- or long-term meteorological phenomena worthy of study, reporting or public advisory such as climate change, storms, heat waves or tornadoes

medtop:20001130.name: weather statistic

medtop:20001133.definition: A genre of music theatre in which singing and dancing play an essential part of the storytelling

medtop:20001134.name: operetta
medtop:20001134.definition: A genre of music theatre that usually has a light or humorous theme where some of the libretto is usually spoken rather than sung.

medtop:20001135.name: art exhibition
medtop:20001135.definition: Temporary presentation of art in museums, art halls or galleries

medtop:20001136.name: trade show or expo
medtop:20001136.definition: Market place to display and trade goods or services

medtop:20001142.name: recreational hiking and climbing

medtop:20001143.name: party
medtop:20001143.definition: A social gathering of invited guests, often involving eating, drinking, dancing or the playing of games

medtop:20001145.name: military service

medtop:20001147.name: sports policies
medtop:20001147.definition: Government policies regulating sports, including sports betting, performance enhancing drug laws and the promition of sports to children for health purposes

medtop:20001148.name: sports transaction
medtop:20001148.definition: The transfer of an athlete from one team to another, the hiring or drafting of an athlete onto a team or the change in professional status of a player on a team

medtop:20001149.name: cross-country skiing
medtop:20001149.definition: Nordic ski race competed in relatively flat, snowy countryside on narrow skis

medtop:20001150.name: Nordic combined
medtop:20001150.definition: Competition combining cross-country skiing and ski jumping

medtop:20001151.name: short track speed skating
medtop:20001151.definition: Races competed by four or more skaters at a time on a small oval ice track

medtop:20001152.name: artistic gymnastics
medtop:20001152.definition: Competitors perform artistic and acrobatic moves on different apparatus and are judged on technical ability and artistic expression

medtop:20001153.name: Telemark skiing
medtop:20001153.definition: Races combining downhill and cross-country skiing events with unique Telemark techniques and equipment

medtop:20001154.name: chess

medtop:20001155.name: roller sports

medtop:20001156.name: skateboarding
medtop:20001156.definition: Competitions involving stunts and acrobatic feats performed on a skateboard using various ramps and other obstacles

medtop:20001157.name: martial arts

medtop:20001158.name: start-up and entrepreneurial business
medtop:20001158.definition: The process of designing, launching and running a new business

medtop:20001159.name: public contract
medtop:20001159.definition: Written contracts between companies and public authorities for the execution of works, the supply of products or the provision of services.

medtop:20001160.name: handicrafts
medtop:20001160.definition: The creators and sellers of crafts and the making and selling of the supplies used to make those crafts

medtop:20001162.name: asset management
medtop:20001162.definition: Managing investments on behalf of others

medtop:20001163.name: client relationship management
medtop:20001163.definition: Creating and maintaining a relationship with the customers to increase sales.

medtop:20001164.name: payment service
medtop:20001164.definition: Services for executing payments including cash, cheque, credit card, debit card, direct debit, electronic funds transfer, internet banking, electronic and mobile payment.

medtop:20001166.name: railway manufacturing
medtop:20001166.definition: Manufactures of rolling stock and suppliers for the maintenance and repair of railroads

medtop:20001167.name: medical equipment
medtop:20001167.definition: Manufacture of medical and surgical devices for diagnosis and treatment such as optical and imaging equipment

medtop:20001168.name: pet product and service
medtop:20001168.definition: Hygiene products, care and nutrition for pets

medtop:20001170.name: logistics
medtop:20001170.definition: Supply chain, inventory management and transportation of products.

medtop:20001171.name: sharing economy
medtop:20001171.definition: Peer-to-peer-based sharing of access to goods and services

medtop:20001172.name: small and medium enterprise
medtop:20001172.definition: A small and medium enterprise (SME) is a company whose number of employees, balance and turnover cannot exceed certain limits set by the country where it is located

medtop:20001174.name: regional development policy
medtop:20001174.definition: Government or private policies, such as business incentives, aimed at the development of a region

medtop:20001175.name: artistic swimming
medtop:20001175.definition: A sport in which swimmers, in solo, duet or team configurations, perform coordinated or identical movements in time to music. They are judged and are awarded points for body position, control, and the degree of difficulty of the moves.

medtop:20001176.name: rugby
medtop:20001176.definition: A form of football played with an oval ball that may be kicked, carried, and passed. Points are scored when one team carries the ball over the other team's goal line or kicks the ball between two goal posts.

medtop:20001177.name: Olympic Games
medtop:20001177.definition: Games organised by the International Olympic Committee and held in summer or winter

medtop:20001178.name: Paralympic Games
medtop:20001178.definition: Games for athletes with disabilities organised by the International Paralympic Committee and held in winter or summer

medtop:20001179.name: series
medtop:20001179.definition: A connected set of fictional or non-fictional program episodes that run under the same title.

medtop:20001180.name: drama (theatre)
medtop:20001180.definition: A genre of theatre where dramatic or comedic plays are performed on the stage

medtop:20001181.name: festival
medtop:20001181.definition: Events showcasing artistic endeavours, often regularly occurring, such as dance, music, theatre, poetry or comedy festivals

medtop:20001182.name: social media
medtop:20001182.definition: Content created to be shared within online social networks

medtop:20001183.name: esports
medtop:20001183.definition: Competitions involving video games often played by professional gamers

medtop:20001184.name: hip hop
medtop:20001184.definition: A genre of music developed in African American communities in the United States in the 1970s which consists of rapping usually with an electronic backing

medtop:20001185.name: r&b
medtop:20001185.definition: A genre of music originated in African American communities in the 1940s and featuring soulful vocals

medtop:20001186.name: heavy metal
medtop:20001186.definition: A genre of loud, aggressive rock music that was developed in the late 1960s and early 1970s

medtop:20001187.name: dance band music
medtop:20001187.definition: A Swedish genre of music characterized by music inspired by swing, schlager, country, jazz and rock that is often danced to in pairs

medtop:20001188.name: electronic dance music
medtop:20001188.definition: A genre of music that employs electronic instruments and is primarily made for nightclubs, raves, and festivals

medtop:20001189.name: children's music
medtop:20001189.definition: A genre of music featuring songs composed and performed for children

medtop:20001190.name: stand-up comedy
medtop:20001190.definition: A comic style in which a comedian performs a series of jokes or stories in front of a live audience, usually speaking directly to them

medtop:20001191.name: cabaret
medtop:20001191.definition: A form of theatrical entertainment featuring music, song, dance, recitation, or drama that is performed in a nightclub or restaurant while the audience eats or drinks at tables

medtop:20001192.name: influencers
medtop:20001192.definition: Persons who distribute content on internet forums and social media and are followed by many people thereby influencing them to buy and use products

medtop:20001193.name: sexual misconduct
medtop:20001193.definition: Unwanted behaviour of a sexual nature that is of lesser offense than felony sexual assault, particularly when behaviour occurs in a normally non-sexual situation, or where there is some aspect of personal power or authority involved

medtop:20001194.name: accounting crime
medtop:20001194.definition: The intentional misrepresentation or alteration of accounting records regarding sales, revenues, expenses and other factors

medtop:20001195.name: tax evasion
medtop:20001195.definition: The illegal evasion of taxes by individuals, corporations, and trusts

medtop:20001196.name: reckless driving
medtop:20001196.definition: Serious traffic violations that are likely to, or have led to, the endangerment, injury or death of a person or persons, or the endangerment of or significant property damage

medtop:20001197.name: administrative law
medtop:20001197.definition: Body of law that governs the actions of governmental administrative agencies

medtop:20001198.name: court-ordered psychiatric treatment
medtop:20001198.definition: Psychiatric treatment imposed upon persons with mental health conditions in prisons and jails or as a condition of probation, supervision or parole

medtop:20001199.name: suspended sentence
medtop:20001199.definition: Legal arrangement where a judge delays the serving of a sentence by a person who has been found guilty of a crime in order to give them a probationary period

medtop:20001200.name: dropped criminal investigation
medtop:20001200.definition: When police and/or prosecutors end an investigation without a conclusion

medtop:20001202.name: wildfire
medtop:20001202.definition: An uncontrolled fire in an area of combustible vegetation

medtop:20001203.name: textile arts
medtop:20001203.definition: Arts and crafts that use plant, animal, or synthetic fibres to construct practical or decorative object

medtop:20001204.name: woodworking
medtop:20001204.definition: The activity or skill of making items, such as furniture or cabinets, from wood

medtop:20001205.name: forging
medtop:20001205.definition: The shaping of metal using localized compressive forces, such as heating and hammering

medtop:20001206.name: self-employment
medtop:20001206.definition: A situation in which an individual works for themselves as a freelancer or business owner instead of working for an employer that pays a salary or a wage

medtop:20001207.name: biofuel
medtop:20001207.definition: Fuel that is derived from biomass, such as ethanol

medtop:20001208.name: geothermal power
medtop:20001208.definition: Thermal energy that is generated and stored in the Earth

medtop:20001209.name: solar power
medtop:20001209.definition: Electricity generated and harvested from the sun's rays

medtop:20001210.name: hydroelectric power
medtop:20001210.definition: Electricity produced from hydropower when water flows through turbines

medtop:20001211.name: wind power
medtop:20001211.definition: Electricity that is generated by kinetic energy of wind, usually produced by windmills or turbines

medtop:20001212.name: religious school
medtop:20001212.definition: School that has a religious component in its operations or its curriculum

medtop:20001213.name: state school
medtop:20001213.definition: Schools maintained by public funds, usually government-imposed taxes

medtop:20001214.name: private school
medtop:20001214.definition: Schools maintained by private funds and organisations

medtop:20001215.name: independent school
medtop:20001215.definition: Schools funded by money from taxes via government, but run by companies, organisations or cooperatives

medtop:20001216.name: vocational education

medtop:20001217.name: educational grading
medtop:20001217.definition: The evaluation of a student's achievement on a test, assignment or course and the policies and methods around assigning those grades

medtop:20001219.name: drug rehabilitation
medtop:20001219.definition: Medical or psychotherapeutic treatment for dependency on substances such as alcohol, prescription and controlled drugs

medtop:20001221.name: emergency care
medtop:20001221.definition: Immediate care of patients with critical medical emergencies, either inside or outside of a hospital

medtop:20001225.name: eye care
medtop:20001225.definition: The medical profession and field of study devoted to diagnosing, preventing and treating eye conditions

medtop:20001228.name: surgery
medtop:20001228.definition: The use of incisions made by medical instruments to investigate or treat a medical condition or injury

medtop:20001229.name: healthcare clinic
medtop:20001229.definition: Local medical facility or doctor's office associated with a general medicine practice, staffed by one or many doctors, focusing on outpatient treatment or giving recommendations to visit a specialist or hospital

medtop:20001230.name: environmental, social and governance policy (ESG)
medtop:20001230.definition: A company's business practices reflecting responsible social, ethical and environmental policies, sometimes known as corporate social responsibility

medtop:20001231.name: mixed martial arts
medtop:20001231.definition: A full-contact combat sport using techniques from various combat sports and martial arts

medtop:20001232.name: elderly care
medtop:20001232.definition: The long-term care of the elderly provided by residential institutions or by paid daily help in the home

medtop:20001233.name: name ceremony
medtop:20001233.definition: Event at which an infant, youth, or adult is given a name

medtop:20001234.name: graduation
medtop:20001234.definition: A ceremony, also known as commencement, at which a person receives a diploma or academic degree

medtop:20001235.name: funeral and memorial service
medtop:20001235.definition: A ceremony to memorialise a deceased person

medtop:20001236.name: wedding
medtop:20001236.definition: Marriage ceremony and the events and parties surrounding it, such as wedding receptions, engagement parties, bridal showers and hen or stag parties

medtop:20001237.name: anniversary
medtop:20001237.definition: The celebration or commemoration of a significant amount of years since an event or a notable person's birth or death

medtop:20001238.name: birthday
medtop:20001238.definition: A celebration on the anniversary of a person's birth.

medtop:20001239.name: exercise and fitness
medtop:20001239.definition: Physical activity with the purpose to maintain and improve health and wellness, gain stamina or for enjoyment

medtop:20001240.name: bodybuilding
medtop:20001240.definition: Competitors perform specific poses to display their muscles that have been strengthened and enlarged through strenuous exercise. Judging is based on criteria such as symmetry, muscularity and conditioning.

medtop:20001241.name: horseback riding
medtop:20001241.definition: The riding of horses for leisure or light exercise.

medtop:20001242.name: steeplechase (athletics)

medtop:20001243.name: oil and gas
medtop:20001243.definition: The exploration, extraction, refining, transporting and marketing of petroleum products and natural gas

medtop:20001244.name: utilities
medtop:20001244.definition: The providing of basic services to the public, such as supplying water, waste removal, heating and cooling

medtop:20001245.name: infrastructure projects
medtop:20001245.definition: The construction of the fundamental facilities and systems serving a country, city, or other area, including roads, bridges, dams, tunnels, telecommunications and electrical grids

medtop:20001247.name: collecting
medtop:20001247.definition: The hobby of seeking, locating, acquiring, organising, cataloguing, displaying, storing or maintaining items that are of interest to an individual collector

medtop:20001248.name: cosmetics
medtop:20001248.definition: Products applied to the body to enhance appearance, such as lipstick, eyeliner, foundation and nail polish, and the trends surrounding the application of these products

medtop:20001249.name: hairstyles
medtop:20001249.definition: Trends surrounding the cutting and styling of hair

medtop:20001250.name: body modification
medtop:20001250.definition: Actions taken to permanently or semi-permanently change body appearance, such as piercing and tattooing

medtop:20001251.name: tattooing
medtop:20001251.definition: A form of body modification where a design is made by inserting ink, dyes and pigments into the dermis layer of the skin to permanently change the pigment

medtop:20001252.name: piercing
medtop:20001252.definition: A form of body modification involving the puncturing or cutting of a part of the human body, creating an opening in which jewellery may be worn or where an implant could be inserted

medtop:20001253.name: cooking and baking
medtop:20001253.definition: Interest in preparing meals or baked goods

medtop:20001254.name: beer, wine and spirits
medtop:20001254.definition: Interest in the consumption, production and collection of alcoholic beverages

medtop:20001257.name: gardening
medtop:20001257.definition: Interest in working in one's garden

medtop:20001258.name: consumer electronics
medtop:20001258.definition: Electronic devices, such as computers, smart phones or televisions, designed and sold for personal use

medtop:20001259.name: political party convention
medtop:20001259.definition: Meeting of political party to nominate a candidate, choose a party leader or set policy

medtop:20001260.name: political committee
medtop:20001260.definition: A legislative sub-group that focuses on a specific area or action

medtop:20001261.name: head of government
medtop:20001261.definition: The highest official in the executive branch of a political entity

medtop:20001262.name: public inquiry
medtop:20001262.definition: An official review of events or actions ordered by a government body, including royal commissions

medtop:20001264.name: infrastructure policy
medtop:20001264.definition: Policies regarding the development and maintenance of the fundamental facilities of a country, city or other area, such as communication, transportation and distribution networks

medtop:20001265.name: local government policy
medtop:20001265.definition: Policies for the development and maintenance of a local government area

medtop:20001266.name: political debates
medtop:20001266.definition: Organised debates between political candidates during their election campaign

medtop:20001267.name: Midsummer
medtop:20001267.definition: Northern European celebrations that accompany the Summer solstice

medtop:20001268.name: National day
medtop:20001268.definition: A designated day to celebrate a nation

medtop:20001269.name: New year
medtop:20001269.definition: The celebration of the end of one calendar year and the start of next

medtop:20001270.name: Halloween
medtop:20001270.definition: A celebration observed in a number of countries on 31 October with activities including trick-or-treating, wearing costumes, carving pumpkins, visiting haunted attractions, telling scary stories and watching horror films

medtop:20001271.name: All Saints Day
medtop:20001271.definition: Christian festival celebrated in honour of all the saints, known and unknown. Holiday is also known as All Hallows' Day, Hallowmas, Feast of All Saints or Solemnity of All Saints.

medtop:20001272.name: Walpurgis night
medtop:20001272.definition: The eve of the Christian feast day of Saint Walpurga, an 8th-century abbess in Francia, celebrated on the night of 30 April and the day of 1 May

medtop:20001273.name: baptism
medtop:20001273.definition: A Christian religious rite, sometimes also called a Christening, involving the sprinkling of holy water onto a person's forehead or immersing them in water, symbolising purification and admission to the Church

medtop:20001274.name: contraception
medtop:20001274.definition: A method or device used to prevent pregnancy

medtop:20001275.name: gig economy
medtop:20001275.definition: a labour market consisting of individual suppliers on short-term contracts or freelance work as opposed to permanent jobs, such as drivers or delivery workers

medtop:20001276.name: parental leave
medtop:20001276.definition: Time off work to give birth or care for a child

medtop:20001277.name: volunteering
medtop:20001277.definition: Unpaid work undertaken freely by individuals as a service to others

medtop:20001278.name: cooperative
medtop:20001278.definition: An organisation which is owned and run jointly by its members, who share the profits or benefits of their work

medtop:20001279.name: cryptocurrency
medtop:20001279.definition: An internet-based medium of exchange using cryptography to conduct financial transactions

medtop:20001280.name: hurricane
medtop:20001280.definition: A type of storm also called a tropical cyclone, which forms over tropical or subtropical waters

medtop:20001282.name: ringette
medtop:20001282.definition: A team sport usually played on ice by skaters using a straight stick. Players pass and shoot a rubber ring in order to place it in the opponent's goal

medtop:20001283.name: human smuggling and trafficking
medtop:20001283.definition: The illegal transporting of people from one country or area to another. When the result is forced labour or sexual exploitation, the crime is considered trafficking.

medtop:20001284.name: bullying
medtop:20001284.definition: Taking actions meant to harm, coerce and intimidate another person perceived as vulnerable. These actions can be taken in person or online.

medtop:20001285.name: vandalism
medtop:20001285.definition: Deliberately damaging or destroying public or private property

medtop:20001286.name: arm wrestling
medtop:20001286.definition: A form of wrestling in which two participants grapple arm-to-arm

medtop:20001287.name: supreme and high court
medtop:20001287.definition: matters related to supreme or high courts, including nominations and rulings

medtop:20001288.name: indigenous people
medtop:20001288.definition: People who are the original owners and caretakers of a given region, also known as native peoples, first peoples or aboriginal peoples, in contrast to groups that have settled, occupied or colonised the area more recently

medtop:20001289.name: sales channel
medtop:20001289.definition: Indirect or direct ways of bringing products or services to market so that they can be purchased by consumers

medtop:20001290.name: public housing
medtop:20001290.definition: Housing that is owned or managed by a government or nonprofit organisation and rented to tenants with the aim of making housing affordable. Eligibility for such housing arrangements varies country to country.

medtop:20001291.name: heating and cooling
medtop:20001291.definition: The business of supplying heat or cooling to private residences and commercial buildings

medtop:20001292.name: economic development incentive
medtop:20001292.definition: The offer of funds, financial incentive programmes or subsidies to stimulate businesses and the economy

medtop:20001293.name: streaming service

medtop:20001294.name: crowdfunding
medtop:20001294.definition: The funding of a project or venture by raising small amounts of money from a large number of people, typically via the internet

medtop:20001295.name: outsourcing
medtop:20001295.definition: Business practice in which services or job functions are farmed out to a third party

medtop:20001296.name: shopping mall
medtop:20001296.definition: A large building or series of connected buildings that contain a variety of retail stores and food vendors

medtop:20001297.name: shopping district and high street
medtop:20001297.definition: Primary retail streets of towns or cities containing individual stores and restaurants

medtop:20001298.name: artificial intelligence
medtop:20001298.definition: An attempt to let computers simulate how the human brain works by applying statistical, heuristic or machine learning methods and algorithms to large datasets. Enables a long range of automatic functions like image recognition and categorisation.

medtop:20001299.name: surveillance
medtop:20001299.definition: Monitoring the activities of the individual through the use of cameras and data in order to prevent or uncover criminal activities

medtop:20001300.name: privacy
medtop:20001300.definition: The right of an individual or group to keep information about themselves private

medtop:20001301.name: sport achievement
medtop:20001301.definition: Records or honours earned by athletes for their performance

medtop:20001302.name: sports record
medtop:20001302.definition: The best performance to date by an athlete or team in a sport discipline

medtop:20001303.name: sports medal and trophy
medtop:20001303.definition: Award given to an athlete or team for placing in a sports competition, such as a gold medal at the Olympics or the Stanley Cup in ice hockey

medtop:20001304.name: sports honour
medtop:20001304.definition: Honour given to a player for achievements over a career, season or single event, unrelated to event outcome, usually awarded by a panel of judges or a popular vote. Examples include player of the game, most valuable player award or hall of fame induction.

medtop:20001305.name: padel
medtop:20001305.definition: Racquet sport typically played in doubles on an enclosed court

medtop:20001306.name: kiting

medtop:20001307.name: stand up paddleboarding (SUP)
medtop:20001307.definition: Water sport using a board and paddle to propel through the water while standing

medtop:20001308.name: krav maga
medtop:20001308.definition: Fighting and self-defence sport that combines elements from aikido, boxing, judo, karate and wrestling developed in Israel

medtop:20001309.name: cheerleading
medtop:20001309.definition: Cheer squads competing against each other to perform a routine that includes stunts, jumps and tumbling set to music. Squads are judged on difficulty and execution.

medtop:20001310.name: kickboxing
medtop:20001310.definition: Stand-up combat sport based on kicking and punching an opponent

medtop:20001311.name: sambo (martial art)
medtop:20001311.definition: Style of martial art originating in the Soviet Union that is recognised as a form of amateur wrestling

medtop:20001312.name: political leadership
medtop:20001312.definition: Positions of leadership within political parties and discussion around whether leadership changes need to be made

medtop:20001313.name: shootings
medtop:20001313.definition: An act of violence committed by individuals with the use of armed weapons

medtop:20001314.name: animal abuse
medtop:20001314.definition: The infliction of cruelty or neglect onto animals by humans

medtop:20001315.name: zoo
medtop:20001315.definition: A park where visitors can see both wild and tame animals that are kept in cages or enclosed areas

medtop:20001316.name: border dispute
medtop:20001316.definition: Diplomatic issues between two countries regarding territorial borders

medtop:20001317.name: child care
medtop:20001317.definition: Services and facilities that look after children while their parents are working or away, including daycare centres and programmes

medtop:20001318.name: pest and pest control
medtop:20001318.definition: Animals or insects that invade a human space causing destruction or unsanitary conditions and the methods for controlling or eradicating them

medtop:20001319.name: disinformation and misinformation
medtop:20001319.definition: The spread of false information regardless of intent

medtop:20001320.name: torture
medtop:20001320.definition: Intentionally inflicting severe physical or psychological pain in order to punish the victim or get the victim to take an action or give information

medtop:20001321.name: drowning
medtop:20001321.definition: When a person's airpipe and lungs become filled with water causing death or injury, most often caused by falling into or bathing in rivers, lakes or the ocean

medtop:20001322.name: poisoning
